headline: Microsoft has published Nobel-winning economist Daron Acemoglu's prediction that AI will lift economic output by only about 1.5% over ten years.
score_reason: Read in full; the forecast is one economist's opinion and he admits the pace is hard to predict. No reduction.
importance_line: Workers and governments planning around AI get a cautious counterweight to bigger claims, though it is one economist's forecast, published by a company that benefits from gradual AI adoption.
summary: The Decoder reports that Microsoft published an essay by Nobel Prize-winning economist Daron Acemoglu predicting AI will raise gross domestic product by about 1.5% over ten years and replace at most 5% of jobs, well below some AI labs' forecasts. He argues the slow part is human: companies must reassign tasks, retrain staff and restructure first, and he admits AI's pace is hard to predict.
notes: Forecast is the economist's opinion, not a measured result.
